newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Telefonica share offer draws to a close.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telefonica share offer draws to a close.

text.p: Investors had a last opportunity on Friday to place orders for shares of Telefonica de Espana, as privatisation of the state's remaining 20.9 percent stake drew to a close.
Retail investors had until 1300 GMT to put in their orders, while national and foreign institutions have up to bourse close at 1600 GMT to place orders for Spain's largest ever placement.
A Telefonica spokesman said the definitive breakdown of the shares to the various tranches will be made public on Monday.
The price of the offer will also be fixed and the operation will be wound up on Tuesday.
At the current price of 3,350 pesetas ($23.39) a share, the public purse would gain revenues of 600 billion pesetas from the sale if all 191.5 million shares are allocated.
Under the terms of the sale, the initial offer consisted of 171 million shares plus a green shoe, or reserve shares, of 20.5 million shares.
In the retail tranche, where small investors receive a four percent bonus holding shares long-term, demand has outstripped the offer by eight times.
As a result, SEPPa, the holding group that administers the state's stake in Telefonica, expanded the offer for this tranche by 17 million shares to 100 million shares.
On Wednesday the company added that it expect the institutional tranche of its public share offering to be 2.8 times over-subscribed.
But the company could decide to direct its green shoe shares to retail investors.

Private investors have not been dissuaded by the shares' high price. Last Friday, SEPPa fixed a maximum price for the retail sale at 3,385 pesetas a share, just 40 pesetas beneath its historic maximum reach on January 22.
But the shares have lately shown signs of fatigue and have lost 35 pesetas a share after rising 4.5 percent last week.
Foreign investors have apparently come to the conclusion that with a price-earnings ratio of 16 for 1997, there are attractive international alternatives to Telefonica.
